questions.q: If we insert two numbers between $\sqrt2$ and 4 so that the resulting sequence is in G.P., then the inserted numbers in the order are
questions.explanation: With common ratio $r$, $4=\sqrt2\cdot r^3 \Rightarrow r^3=2\sqrt2 \Rightarrow r=\sqrt2$. The inserted terms are $\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt2=2$ and $2\cdot\sqrt2=2\sqrt2$.

If the middle term of the A.P is 300 then the sum of its first 51 terms is
questions.explanation: For 51 terms, the middle (26th) term equals the average term, so sum = 51 $\times$ 300 = 15300.

questions.q: If the sum of $n$ terms of an A.P. is given by $S_n = n^2 + n$, then the common difference of the A.P. is
questions.explanation: $a_n = S_n - S_{n-1} = n^2+n-[(n-1)^2+(n-1)] = 2n$, so the common difference is $2$.

questions.q: The third term of a G.P. is 9. The product of its first five terms is
questions.explanation: The product of the first five terms equals $(ar^2)^5=9^5=3^{10}$.

questions.q: If a, b, c are three consecutive terms of an AP and x, y, z are three consecutive terms of a GP, then the value of $x^{b-c}\cdot y^{c-a}\cdot z^{a-b}$ is
questions.explanation: Since $xz=y^2$ (GP) and exponents sum to zero using the AP condition, the expression simplifies to 1.
This is an AP with first term 3 and common difference 2; sum $=\dfrac n2[2(3)+(n-1)2]=n(n+2)$.

questions.q: The sum of $1^{st}$ n terms of the series $\dfrac{1^2}{1}+\dfrac{1^2+2^2}{1+2}+\dfrac{1^2+2^2+3^2}{1+2+3}+\ldots$
questions.explanation: The $k$-th term is $\dfrac{k(k+1)(2k+1)/6}{k(k+1)/2}=\dfrac{2k+1}{3}$; summing this from $k=1$ to $n$ gives $\dfrac{n(n+2)}{3}$.

questions.explanation: From $a/(1-r)=4$ and $ar=3/4$, solving gives $r=1/4, a=3$ (or $r=3/4,a=1$); option (1) is listed.

questions.q: The sum of the series $\dfrac{1}{2\cdot3}\cdot2+\dfrac{2}{3\cdot4}\cdot2^2+\dfrac{3}{4\cdot5}\cdot2^3+\ldots$ to n terms is
questions.explanation: The general term telescopes as $b_{k+1}-b_k$ with $b_k=\dfrac{2^k}{k+1}$, giving the sum $\dfrac{2^{n+1}}{n+2}-1$.
The $r$-th term is $\dfrac{\sum_{k=1}^r k^2}{\sum_{k=1}^r k}=\dfrac{2r+1}{3}$. Summing from $r=1$ to $n$ gives $\dfrac{n^2+2n}{3}=\dfrac{n(n+2)}{3}$.

questions.q: The $n^{th}$ term of the series $1+3+7+13+21+\ldots$ is 9901. The value of $n$ is
questions.explanation: The $n^{th}$ term is $T_n=n^2-n+1$. Setting $n^2-n+1=9901$ gives $n^2-n-9900=0$, whose positive root is $n=100$.
